bibl.title: A reflection on the use of artificial intelligence tools for the meaningful learning of mathematics

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: prediction
span.quote: By complementing, rather than replacing, traditional teaching methods, AI can play a significant role in transforming mathematics education for the better, helping to create more dynamic, inclusive and effective learning environments for all students.

span.label: AI tools in mathematics education
span.quote: Meaningful learning in mathematics goes beyond rote memorisation of formulas or the mechanical application of algorithms.

span.label: review
span.quote: This editorial examines the potential impact of AI tools on fostering deeper understanding in mathematics, while also addressing the challenges associated with their implementation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AI systems continuously re-tune problem difficulty to the individual student's measured performance, holding each learner at a level of challenge that is neither too easy nor too hard, which is the route by which personalisation is claimed to produce deeper learning
span.quote: For instance, adaptive learning platforms adjust the difficulty of problems based on the student’s performance, ensuring that they are neither overwhelmed nor under-stimulated.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: immediate machine feedback lets a learner detect and repair an error while the attempt is still active, so the correct concept is reinforced instead of the mistake being consolidated
span.quote: Moreover, AI-driven systems can offer immediate feedback, allowing learners to correct their mistakes in real-time and reinforcing key concepts.

span.label: The subject is introduced by equating three different things - a field, a capability and a class of model - in the editorial's first sentence.
span.quote: Artificial intelligence (AI), also known as generative AI and large language models, has steadily emerged as a transformative force across various sectors of daily life

span.label: The term the whole argument rests on is given only by what it exceeds, never by a criterion that would decide a case.
span.quote: Meaningful learning in mathematics goes beyond rote memorisation of formulas or the mechanical application of algorithms

span.label: The editorial's own caveat is that the technology may displace the teacher rather than assist them.
span.quote: One concern is the potential for over-reliance on AI tools, which may lead to a diminished role for teachers (Harry & Sayudin, 2023). While AI can automate certain tasks, the human element of teaching – such as providing emotional support, fostering critical thinking and encouraging collaboration – remains irreplaceable (García-Martínez et al., 2023). Therefore, AI should be seen as a tool that complements, rather than replaces, the teacher’s role in facilitating meaningful learning

span.label: Access to the technology is named as a precondition for any of the claimed benefits.
span.quote: Ensuring equitable access to AI technology is essential if it is to have a positive impact on meaningful learning in mathematics

span.label: meaningful learning - DEFINED BY NEGATION: what it goes beyond (rote memorisation, mechanical application of algorithms) rather than by any property that would let a reader decide whether a given lesson achieved it
span.quote: Meaningful learning in mathematics goes beyond rote memorisation of formulas or the mechanical application of algorithms

span.label: artificial intelligence - AS THREE NAMES FOR ONE THING: the editorial's opening sentence treats AI, generative AI and large language models as interchangeable, which is the conflation every later claim inherits
span.quote: Artificial intelligence (AI), also known as generative AI and large language models

span.label: personalisation - AS THE PROPOSED MECHANISM: customised learning paths tailored to each student's strengths, weaknesses and pace, which is what the editorial means when it says AI supports meaningful learning
span.quote: Artificial intelligence tools can address this challenge by offering customised learning paths tailored to each student’s strengths, weaknesses and learning pace

span.label: builds-on → How & Hung (2019)
span.quote: However, the integration of AI into education also raises critical questions regarding its effectiveness, accessibility and ethical implications (How & Hung, 2019).

span.label: The editorial's central position is that AI should be treated as a supplement to the teacher rather than a substitute, because the human side of teaching cannot be automated.
span.quote: Therefore, AI should be seen as a tool that complements, rather than replaces, the teacher’s role in facilitating meaningful learning.

span.label: It argues that leaning too heavily on tools such as ChatGPT may stunt students' development of their own problem-solving skills.
span.quote: However, there are concerns that over-reliance on AI tools such as ChatGPT might undermine students’ ability to develop their own problem-solving skills (Grájeda et al., 2024).

span.label: It warns that unequal access to AI tools risks widening rather than narrowing educational inequality.
span.quote: The digital divide could exacerbate existing educational inequalities, particularly in under-resourced communities.

span.label: It identifies student data collection by AI platforms as an unresolved ethical and privacy problem for schools.
span.quote: Artificial intelligence tools often collect large amounts of data on students’ performance and behaviour, raising questions about how these data are used and who has access to it (Pedró, 2020).

span.quote: Meaningful learning in mathematics goes beyond rote memorisation of formulas or the mechanical application of algorithms.

span.label: ChatGPT
span.quote: One AI tool gaining popularity among mathematics educators is ChatGPT, an advanced conversational AI model developed by OpenAI.

span.label: artificial intelligence (AI)
span.quote: Artificial intelligence (AI), also known as generative AI and large language models, has steadily emerged as a transformative force across various sectors of daily life, including education.
